inclusion_criteria: Peer-reviewed articles, conference papers, and vetted arXiv preprints with methods and evaluation details
Works published from 2018 to present (to cover modern ML + LLM era), prioritizing 2020–2026 for LLM-specific studies
Papers describing tools, validators, simulators, or datasets applicable to network configuration or NetOps workflows
Empirical studies with reproducible artifacts (code, data, or clear protocols) where available
Standards, guidance, and operator postmortems relevant to production NetOps safety and incident analyses
Surveys and systematic reviews of AIOps, network verification, or LLM safety that synthesize prior evidence
exclusion_criteria: Non-technical news articles, marketing pages, or opinion pieces without methodological detail
Works unrelated to networks/NetOps (pure NLP without systems or configuration context)
Non-English sources unless they provide unique, verifiable technical content and translations are available
Proprietary internal reports or private datasets unavailable for public validation
Duplicate versions where a higher-quality peer-reviewed version exists (prefer primary source)
date_rationale: Include literature from 2018–present to capture the surge in ML-for-systems and the LLM era (notably 2020 onward). Earlier (pre-2018) formal verification and network-theory foundations may be included selectively, but emphasis will be on 2020–2026 work to reflect LLM-specific mechanisms, agentic frameworks, and recent benchmarks.
